name: Emai-Iuleha-Ora
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Egbokhare, F. O. 1990. A phonology of Emai (PhD, Ibadan); Schaefer & Egbokhare 2017. A grammar of Emai (Mouton, paywalled)
earlier_scan.note: Full grammar and phonology thesis exist (tonal Edoid language); neither openly readable

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2022. Secondary concepts and internal dynamics of Emai serial verb constructions. Stellenbosch Papers in Linguistics Plus 65. doi:10.5842/65-1-976
sources.note: Only orthographic tone conventions (acute = high, grave = low, acute+downstep) and 'non-contour, level tones (high or low) on polysyllabic verbs'; no stress.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. 2013. Demarcating Emai dative constructions. Studies in African Linguistics 42(1). doi:10.32473/sal.v42i1.107275; Schaefer & Egbokhare 2021 Metatony (PLSA 6, doi:10.3765/plsa.v6i1.5000); Schaefer & Egbokhare 2023 Preverbs (PLSA 8, doi:10.3765/plsa.v8i1.5507); Schaefer 1986 Reference point marking in Emai (ERIC ED285405); Schaefer & Egbokhare 2002 Emai sentence complements (ERIC ED468597)
sources.note: Syntax/semantics papers; each only restates the tone-marking convention (high = acute, low = grave, downstep = acute + apostrophe); grep for stress/accent/prominence finds nothing relevant in any of them.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 1994. Emai verbal and preverbal tone: preliminaries. Paper, 25th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, New Brunswick, March 1994. ERIC ED375640, 16 pp.
sources.note: Tone only: 'two significant level tones low and high', rising/falling from juxtaposition; verbs, auxiliaries and monosyllabic preverbs are lexically toneless and get surface tone by rule. Zero mentions of stress/accent/prominence (only 'accent' in a reference title).

sources.citation: WALS Online, language 'Emai' (wals code ora, glottocode emai1241), sources Donwa-Ifode 1990 and Schaefer & Egbokhare 2007.
sources.note: Emai is coded for 11 WALS features (10A, 81A-95A, 116A) but NOT for the stress chapters 14A-17A; no secondary stress datum exists.

sources.citation: Donwa-Ifode, Shirley O. 1990. Transitional phonologies and their implication for orthographies: the case of Ora. Journal of West African Languages 20(2): 3-18.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Segmental sketch of Ora ('My data is based on Emai', p. 3): 7 oral + 7 nasal vowel phonemes, consonant inventory, vowel sequences, nasalisation, orthography. Tone appears only in the discussion of the floating high-tone genitival linker (pp. 15-16). Nothing on stress, accent or prominence.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2026. Mood: tonal and segmental realization in Edoid. Proceedings of the Linguistic Society of America 11(1). doi:10.3765/plsa.v11i1.6059
sources.note: Grammatical tone of the 'predicative complex' (H/L two-tone structures over lexically toneless subject/tense segments; 'tono-exodus'). 'Prominence' occurs only as 'mood prominence' (Bhat). No stress statement.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2024. Tone, viewpoint aspect, and imperative mood. Proceedings of the Linguistic Society of America 9(1). doi:10.3765/plsa.v9i1.5657
sources.note: High tone spread / lowering of the verb-phrase-initial syllable as aspect-mood exponents; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2021. Edo North: refugium and micro-accretion zone. Abstract, SLE 2021.
sources.note: Areal note only: 'Tone systems contrast high vs. low, with downstep addition in more southerly areas and mid tone west of center.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory 707 'emai' (AA), from Hartell (ed.) 1993 / Chanard 2006.
sources.note: 48 segments; no tone or suprasegmental information.

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Oisa-Francis. 1989. Phono-semantic correspondence in deictics in Emai. Journal of West African Languages 19(1).
sources.note: Morphophonology of deictics (V1-CV2-(V3) templates); no statement on stress or on the tone system.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2019. Class marking in Emai: retention, reduction, and transformation of inherited morphology, ch. 1 'Emai, Edoid, and Benue Congo'. Lanham: Lexington Books / Bloomsbury.

sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked
sources.note: Publisher page says the grammatical sketch covers orthography, pronunciation and 'tonal variations'; a pronunciation section is where a stress remark would appear. archive.org copy is lending-only (full text 401, search-inside unavailable); Köppe sells a PDF.

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Oisaghaede Francis. 1990. A phonology of Emai. PhD thesis, University of Ibadan. xvii+396 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of the language (Glottolog hhtype phonology); a 396-page thesis by a native-speaker linguist is the likeliest place for an explicit statement on stress vs tone. Not in the Ibadan institutional repository; no online copy found.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiomamhe. 1989. Comparative Edoid: phonology and lexicon (Delta Series 6). Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The standard comparative phonology of Edoid; its synchronic chapters on tone and syllable structure may state for the family (and Ora-Emai-Iuleha specifically) that word prominence is tonal with no stress. Not online.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. 1987. An initial orthography and lexicon for Emai, an Edoid language of Nigeria. Bloomington: Indiana University Linguistics Club.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Earliest orthographic/phonological statement on Emai, the source of the tone-marking conventions used in every later paper; a lexicon with pronunciation notes could state whether stress is marked or absent. HathiTrust search-only (uva.x001561151) but full-text search is Cloudflare-walled from our machine.
